papers.title: Agent Name Collision Attacks in Multi-Agent Systems
papers.abstract: Multi-agent hosts turn remote Agent Cards into local agents, tools, workflow targets, and broker routes. A2A defines the card's name as human-readable metadata, not as a stable identity, and specifies no collision semantics. The security failure begins when a host nevertheless uses that remote name as a local routing identifier. We traced registration through dispatch and ran isolated regression tests at seven pinned open-source revisions. Six client-style integrations selected an attacker-controlled peer's client or loopback endpoint for a request addressed to a trusted peer's name. A seventh, brokered implementation collapsed both peers onto one name-derived route; queue and access-control state determine whether the result is interception or denial. The common result is wrong-peer dispatch, not universal privilege inheritance. Synthetic credential and tool tests found no A-specific credential transfer in the tested client bindings and no direct transfer of A-owned tools. The broker path forwards a caller-configuration object; delegated identity or tokens reach B only if present and B can consume the route. Two other paths expose a later, model-mediated decision rather than direct execution authority. The necessary conditions assign different responsibilities to the protocol, implementations, and deployments. Hosts should route by an origin-bound stable identity, keep names presentational, and reject ambiguous aliases. The evidence establishes a recurring implementation vulnerability class, not a universal A2A protocol exploit or a count of vulnerable deployments.
papers.llm_summary: Chỉ ra lỗ hổng Agent Name Collision trong hệ multi-agent (A2A): host dùng tên card làm ID định tuyến dẫn tới dispatch nhầm peer, test regression trên 7 repo open-source thật.
papers.llm_reason: Trực tiếp về agent architecture (33/35), experiment thực tế trên mã nguồn thật (23/25), có hướng dẫn hardening cụ thể (route by origin-bound stable identity) rất actionable cho ai tự build agent pipeline (17/20).

papers.title: RAG-Safety-Bench: Reliable Evaluation of Retrieval-Augmented LLM Safety
papers.abstract: Allowing large language models (LLMs) to retrieve information from a set of trusted documents can increase reliability and reduce hallucination. However, recent work has demonstrated that retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) can have unintended side effects on the overall safety of the generated responses, when prompted for harmful or dangerous content. A clearer understanding of the mechanisms leading to this result is needed, as increasing numbers of end users turn to RAG to incorporate corporate documents and knowledge bases into LLM-based systems. We introduce RAG-Safety-Bench, a benchmark to measure the safety impact of RAG on LLM models. By removing the confounding effect of retriever quality, and cleanly separating the problem into four conditions -- non-RAG, RAG with an oracle document containing the answer to the harmful request, RAG with documents related to the harmful request but without the specific answer, and RAG with random, safe documents -- the benchmark isolates the impacts of different factors in the observed safety degradation. We report results across five open-source LLMs, showing an inverse relationship between benign and unsafe capability, strong evidence that baseline safety guardrails do not lead to downstream safety guarantees in the RAG case, and model-specific support for previous findings that even benign documents can lead to unsafe generation in retrieval-enabled systems.
papers.llm_summary: Giới thiệu RAG-Safety-Bench — benchmark đo lường tác động an toàn của RAG lên LLM bằng cách tách biệt 4 điều kiện (không RAG, RAG oracle, RAG related, RAG random) trên 5 LLM open-source, phát hiện guardrails baseline không đảm bảo an toàn khi có retrieval và ngay cả tài liệu vô hại cũng có thể gây unsafe generation.
papers.llm_reason: Rất liên quan RAG/LLM safety; experiment chặt chẽ với controlled benchmark; trực tiếp liên quan business vì ngày càng nhiều doanh nghiệp dùng RAG với knowledge bases; insight cực kỳ actionable — hiểu rằng RAG có thể phá vỡ safety guardrails, cần audit riêng cho RAG pipeline.

papers.title: System X: An LLM Decision Model That Replies from Its Own KV Cache
papers.abstract: Decision models return probabilities over supplied options, but a deployed agent may also need to reply in words. The present study introduces System X, a large language model (LLM) decision model that adds a text-reply option to the LLM-as-Jev readout. When this option wins, or confidence is low, the same model continues from the decision's key-value (KV) cache, avoiding a repeated prompt prefill. Qwen3-0.6B has been fine-tuned with LoRA on Reason-9k and Bitext reply rows. JevBench accuracy shows no statistically significant change (55.4% to 54.5%, p=0.87), while expected calibration error falls from 0.292 to 0.169. Held-out Bitext routing accuracy reaches 98.3%. Cache reuse saves 15-37% of latency on an Apple M4 Pro, with token-identical replies in the FP32 demonstration cases. Scoring options on copies of the prompt cache matches full-sequence scoring to within 1.4e-6 in probability. Adding dialogue, industry and complaint data (System X+) improves support-task results but lowers IFEval accuracy from 55.5% to 45.0%. System X v4 uses Qwen3-1.7B, rebalanced data and teacher-rewritten reply targets. Against its base LLM, JevBench accuracy rises from 55.0% to 61.0% (p=0.04), with no statistically significant IFEval change (p=0.71). A matched latency test on unadapted Qwen3-1.7B saves 17-39%. One LLM judge prefers v4 replies to an unadapted 1.7B second call (31 to 11 pairs, p=0.003); the other's preference is not significant. These reply comparisons also differ in prompts and generation limits. State conflicts and unsupported reply details remain failure modes. Further studies with several seeds, human raters and real support data are recommended.
papers.llm_summary: Giới thiệu System X, một LLM decision model có thể reply từ KV cache của chính nó, giúp tiết kiệm 15-39% latency mà không giảm chất lượng.
papers.llm_reason: Rất liên quan vì tối ưu chi phí vận hành LLM, tiết kiệm latency và chi phí inference — solopreneur chạy nhiều kênh AI sẽ được lợi trực tiếp từ kỹ thuật cache reuse này.

papers.title: Physical Agentic AI: An Architecture for Orchestrating a Robot Crew with LLMs
papers.abstract: Agentic AI frameworks interpret open-ended task goals and decompose them into multi-step plans. Richer information about embodiment-specific capabilities, physical preconditions, and cross-robot coordination improves grounding, but does not eliminate infeasible, mistimed, or unsafe physical actions. Physical robot crews therefore require an explicit architectural interface between semantic planning and execution, where every planned action is verified against robot capabilities, system state, and workflow constraints before actuation. This paper introduces Physical Agentic AI, a framework for skill-grounded robot agent orchestration, in which each robot exposes a typed library of executable skills while a foundation model planner decomposes a task into phases and assigns each phase to a robot-skill pair. A Robot Orchestration layer exposes the skill library, robot state, named locations, and workflow contracts to a non-actuating Mission Planner, while a deterministic Robot Orchestrator validates and authorizes one skill at a time. We evaluate on a drone-UGV search-and-dispatch mission, where every mission in every condition is executed live in Gazebo, and on a humanoid-quadruped transportation task using hardware-equivalent skill interfaces plus two physical trials on a Unitree G1 and Go2. Varying planner knowledge and runtime enforcement independently, we find that retrieval raises skill grounding from 51% to 96% yet leaves informed planners dispatching 23-29% of faulted steps. Per-dispatch enforcement reduces false dispatch to 0% with no false blocks, and a held-plan ablation confirms that the gate, not plan variation, is responsible. Live execution makes the difference physical: without enforcement all eight injected faults crossed the orchestration boundary and six produced robot motion; with enforcement all eight were refused before motion.
papers.llm_summary: Kiến trúc Physical Agentic AI tách planner LLM khỏi orchestrator tất định, kiểm chứng từng skill robot trước khi hành động, thử nghiệm thật trên Gazebo và robot Unitree.
papers.llm_reason: Đúng trọng tâm agentic/tool-skill use, experiment phần cứng thật, và cho lesson hành động rõ (planner≠executor, skill-grounding) áp dụng được cho nội dung về agent.

papers.title: Automated Multi-Agent Organization Design: From Architecture Search to Organizational Learning
papers.abstract: Agentic system design is increasingly shifting from hand-crafted prompts and workflows toward automated search over agentic programs and interaction structures, with multi-agent systems receiving growing attention. Yet a central question remains unresolved: when does an automatically generated multi-agent structure exhibit a functionally meaningful division of responsibility? We argue that automated multi-agent design should move beyond searching for effective architectures toward identifying which responsibilities are functionally necessary, how they should be allocated, and when they should change. To explore this, we propose Automated Multi-Agent Organization Design (AMOD), which treats organization itself as a first-class design object, explicitly modeling how agent teams are composed, what functional responsibilities the agents assume, how they coordinate, and how collective decisions are made. We formulate AMOD as an execution-driven design loop. For each task, an automated designer instantiates an organization by assigning functional responsibilities and coordination rules to a set of agents. After execution, task outcomes, intermediate artifacts, and interaction traces are examined to identify which responsibilities may be missing, duplicated, or ineffective, and the organization is revised accordingly. We also propose testing discovered responsibilities by removing them, replacing them with generic roles, or changing their assignment under matched resource budgets, with complementary evaluations. AMOD provides a principled foundation for evidence-based and adaptive multi-agent organization design.
papers.llm_summary: Đề xuất AMOD, framework tự động thiết kế tổ chức multi-agent xem xét tổ chức là đối tượng thiết kế bậc nhất, mô hình hóa thành phần agent, phân bổ trách nhiệm, phối hợp và ra quyết định tập thể qua vòng lặp execution-driven.
papers.llm_reason: Rất liên quan multi-agent system design; khái niệm organization design, responsibility allocation, coordination rules map trực tiếp vào tư duy xây dựng workflow AI cho content business; insight actionable cao.

papers.title: Prospective Interpretation Risk: Principled Communication Control Between LLMs
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agentic systems increasingly rely on models communicating with one another, yet existing uncertainty and multi-agent methods rarely estimate how a particular receiver will interpret a message before it is sent. This matters in heterogeneous systems, where capable receivers can reconstruct different tasks from the same message. We model this as a sender-receiver problem with a latent receiver type and define prospective interpretation risk (PIR): the probability that a receiver reconstructs a task other than intended. Rather than model an LLM's full input-output behaviour, we use black-box probes relating messages, intended tasks, and receiver-specific reconstructions, yielding scalable supervision while separating interpretation from downstream capability failure. Offline, heterogeneous frozen receivers provide supervision for receiver-conditioned risk and the effects of predefined mutable message features. At deployment, history induces a posterior over receiver types, guiding message revision and selection. We introduce value of interpretation information (VoII), querying for receiver information only when its expected communication benefit exceeds its cost. Our theory characterises when receiver information has decision value and bounds such queries. Empirically, interpretation-failure rates vary by 4-13x across receivers. Receiver information reduces PIR calibration error by 68% relative to a receiver-agnostic predictor, largely by correcting receiver-specific risk levels. PIR-guided revision reduces interpretation failure by 44% relative to the original message and 40% relative to a generic rewrite, mostly through a repair that helps every receiver. VoII outperforms information-gain and random querying at matched cost on the interpretation objective it optimises, lowering interpretation failure from 3.84% to 3.79% while querying 18.2% of episodes.
papers.llm_summary: Đo lường rủi ro LLM agent 'hiểu sai' tin nhắn của agent khác trước khi gửi, dùng probe hộp đen và chỉ hỏi thông tin receiver khi lợi ích vượt chi phí (VoII).
papers.llm_reason: Cực kỳ phù hợp multi-agent/tool-use (32/35) với experiment thật (biến thiên 4-13x giữa các receiver), giúp solopreneur thiết kế prompt/pipeline agent nhiều bước ít bị 'service khác hiểu sai task' (17/20 actionable).

papers.title: Procedural Graphs: Self-Evolving Execution Structures for LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Large language models are increasingly deployed as agents that plan over long horizons and act through external tools. Most agents select actions through unconstrained generation over an accumulating history, leaving implicit the procedural knowledge of what to do, in what order, and under which conditions. As trajectories lengthen, agents can lose track of their objectives, invoke tools out of order, and repeat unproductive actions. We introduce the Procedural Graph: just as a knowledge graph organizes factual knowledge into (entity, relation, entity) triplets for what-is questions, a Procedural Graph organizes procedural knowledge into (procedure, relation, procedure) triplets for what-to-do questions. At each decision step, the framework localizes the agent's active node, and a guidance model translates the surrounding subgraph into step-level situational guidance that biases the solver's next action without dictating it. The graph is self-evolving: an LLM refiner contrasts failed trajectories with successful ones and edits the graph's topology and attributes, committing edits that preserve or improve held-out validation performance while retaining rejected ones to discourage repetition. Starting from a minimal skeleton, the loop builds graphs that match or surpass hand-designed ones. It can also repair a flawed expert prior. Across multiple datasets, task types, and LLMs, the Procedural Graph delivers consistent gains over memory-based baselines, and self-evolution further improves performance without manual engineering.
papers.llm_summary: Giới thiệu Procedural Graph — cấu trúc đồ thị tự tiến hóa tổ chức tri thức thủ tục (what-to-do) cho LLM agents, dùng mô hình hướng dẫn dịch subgraph thành step-level guidance và tự sửa graph từ trajectory thành công/thất bại, đạt hoặc vượt graph thiết kế thủ công.
papers.llm_reason: Rất liên quan LLM agents, tool-use, planning; có experiment đa dataset/model; insight 'tự xây dựng graph quy trình từ thất bại' truyền cảm hứng cho việc thiết kế workflow AI automation tốt hơn trong content production.

papers.title: HydraLLM: Adaptive Width Slicing for Elastic Text and Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract: LLMs and LVLMs are increasingly deployed across heterogeneous hardware, ranging from data-center GPUs to resource-constrained edge devices. Their fixed-size architectures limit the ability to reuse a single model across deployment settings with different compute, latency, and model-size targets. We introduce HydraLLM, an elastic MQA-based architecture. Its number of active attention heads determines the effective widths of the embeddings, attention projections, feed-forward layers, and the output head, forming a nested family of subnetworks within a single parameter set. We introduce a static-to-elastic conversion pipeline that, starting from a pre-trained model checkpoint, includes importance-driven weight reordering and stochastic subnetwork training with knowledge distillation. We extend this principle to multimodal inference through an elastic projection module whose output width follows the active text width. HydraLLM covers a wider range of active parameter configurations than FFN-only elastic architectures. With 75% of heads active, HydraLLM achieves 2.2 percentage points higher TriviaQA accuracy than a state-of-the-art nested baseline configuration which has 17.25% more parameters. With 50% of heads active, our multimodal model achieves a CLIPScore comparable to that of the 7$\times$ larger Gemma 3 4B model. With only 25% of heads active, HydraLLM increases token-generation throughput by 75.3% over the full-width configuration.
papers.llm_summary: HydraLLM tạo một mô hình LLM/VLM "co giãn" được: bật ít attention head hơn để chạy trên nhiều loại hardware (GPU数据中心 đến edge) mà vẫn giữ chất lượng.
papers.llm_reason: Cực kỳ relevant AI/LLM (kiến trúc弹性, MQA), benchmark thật (TriviaQA, CLIPScore so Gemma 3 4B), nhưng ít chạm trực tiếp marketing/content; insight chủ yếu là cách chọn size model để tiết kiệm chi phí triển khai cho solopreneur.

papers.title: LLM-Based Multi-Agent Collaboration for Constrained Multi-Objective Container Placement
papers.abstract: Container placement in data centers must simultaneously minimize power consumption and maximize affinity preferences, while satisfying multi-resource capacity and anti-affinity constraints. Traditional approaches typically rely on fixed rules, which lack adaptability to dynamic cluster states and are difficult to extend for adaptive decision-making. On the other hand, meta-heuristic methods, although more flexible, are often computationally expensive, slower and prone to getting trapped in local optima. In this work, we propose an adaptive and efficient approach based on an LLM-driven multi-agent collaboration framework, where four specialized agents operate in a closed-loop ReAct cycle at each placement step. A Power Consumption Agent and an Affinity Agent debate over competing objectives, while a Placement Agent resolves conflicts using Tolerance-Gated Arbitration (TGA). A Rearrangement Agent further refines decisions through the Monotone Improvement Rule (MIR) in a post-placement refinement phase. All the agents reason over deterministic, feasibility-filtered candidate tables provided by the environment, ensuring that every proposed action inherently satisfies hard constraints. Based on experimental evaluation using the Google Cluster Trace with a configuration of 100 applications and 25 machines, the proposed framework consumes 8.36% less power and achieves 39.30% higher affinity than the power-greedy baseline. Ablation studies confirm that each architectural component, the multi-round debate mechanism, the TGA in the Placement Agent, and the MIR in the Rearrangement Agent, contributes meaningfully to the overall performance, with removal of any single component degrading both power consumption and affinity satisfaction.
papers.llm_summary: Framework multi-agent ReAct với 4 chuyên gia (Power, Affinity, Placement, Rearrangement) tranh luận và arbitrage để tối ưu placement container, tiết kiệm 8.36% điện.
papers.llm_reason: Mô hình debate + arbitration giữa các agent chuyên biệt rất sát với cách solopreneur cân bằng các KPI (lượng truy cập, engagement, doanh thu) trên nhiều kênh; có benchmark thực.

papers.title: CLASHarness: Benchmarking Multi-Agent Conflict in Computer Use via a Controllable and Verifiable Generation Pipeline
papers.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) are increasingly deployed in multi-agent systems to automate complex computer-use workflows, yet existing benchmarks mostly assume consistent, cooperative environments. In contrast, real-world collaboration rarely runs on consistent information: peer or sub-agents frequently report outdated states, issue contradictory instructions, or compete over shared permissions and files, forcing agents to check others' outputs and verify ground truth in the environment. Evaluating such conflict resolution remains challenging: manual authoring cannot scale across complex systems, while unconstrained LLM generation produces narrative drift, answer leakage, and unsatisfiable rubrics. We introduce CLASHarness (Conflict-Loaded Agent Scenario Harness), a controllable framework for generating verifiable multi-agent conflicts in computer use, with a benchmark of 600 multi-round tasks. By combining hierarchical scenario planning with an eight-step verified micro-pipeline, CLASHarness pre-commits decisive visual facts before rendering and compiles hybrid code and semantic graders directly from executed reference trajectories, guaranteeing every task is solvable by construction. Evaluating 15 frontier models on CLASHarness reveals three core bottlenecks. First, when sub-agent outputs conflict with the environment, weaker models blindly follow misleading information, whereas stronger models inspect visual evidence to verify ground truth. Second, resolving conflicts is much harder than finding them: while agents can spot inconsistencies, actively fixing system state drops task success significantly. Third, coordination protocols remain a universal bottleneck: even frontier models fail over 58% of closing actions, often forgetting to release shared locks or hand off tasks. CLASHarness provides a scalable, verifiable foundation for building reliable multi-agent systems.
papers.llm_summary: Xây dựng CLASHarness, benchmark 600 task multi-round đánh giá khả năng xử lý xung đột của multi-agent VLM trong computer use, phát hiện 3 bottleneck cốt lõi bao gồm việc model yếu mù quáng theo thông tin sai lệch từ sub-agent.
papers.llm_reason: Multi-agent conflict cực kỳ relevant trend (33/35), benchmark quy mô lớn 15 model (23/25), findings rất dễ chuyển thành content viral về giới hạn AI agents (10/20 business, 10/20 actionable).
